_desc: ★ THE R3 GATE FOR §3/T6 (spec 2026-07-27-team-plane-static-parity-routing-design, owner ruling §11): a TEAM-plane message must not generate a STATIC-plane frame. This is the ONE configuration s35a/s35b cannot cover — they are OFF-GRID only (which is exactly why their A2/A4 are labelled algebra-only in-file), and the defect T6 fixes only exists for a HOMED member. 4 nodes on ONE PHY, ONE leaf nibble (mixed-leaf is s29/s35a's axis, not this one). ★ THE LOAD-BEARING TOPOLOGY, and every link is deliberate: TH is a HOMED member (it hears H1, registers, and its _node_id becomes the host-assigned mobile local id while its team id stays 210); TO is an OFF-GRID member with NO LINK TO H1 AT ALL, so TO holds no static route to 101 and cannot acquire one — TH is is_mobile, so route_uses_mobile_as_transit refuses it as static transit. That absence is the whole experiment: it converts the pre-T6 plane crossing from a silent success into a LOUD, countable failure. Pre-T6 (measured 2026-07-28, BASELINE SCEN note): stamp_origin gave a homed member's team DM origin = its HOME's STATIC id 101, the acking teammate took origin as its ack destination and addressed 101 on the STATIC plane — r_tx{dst:101,reason:no_route} at ttl 1 then ttl 16 x3 (FOUR static RREQ floods generated by a TEAM message's ack), send_deferred_giveup, then send_failed{e2e_ack_timeout} on TH at +60 s. Post-T6 the origin is 210, AUTO dispatches it to _rt_team via is_team_peer, and the ack returns on the team plane in ~1 s with zero static frames. ★ THE CONTROL ARM IS TO->TH (asserts 20-23), the off-grid direction, which worked BEFORE T6 and must still work AFTER: without it a green run could not distinguish 'T6 fixed the homed case' from 'the acks happen to work now'. ⚠ TWO AUTHORING TRAPS, both hit while building this file. (1) team_dad_pin_id is REQUIRED, not cosmetic: without it team-DAD picks uniformly at random from 17..254, so no assertion could name an origin id and the R3 assertion could not be written at all. It pins only the FIRST pick (node_mobile.cpp:188) and a re-pick still randomises, so convergence is untouched. (2) `-t` is a TRAILING suffix on both send verbs (sim NodeRuntimeWrapper, committed 8135912) — the prefix form silently airs '-t <text>' as the BODY on plane AUTO, which is the defect that was live in s23:25/31/37/43 until 2026-07-28. ⚠ DO NOT read `rt_update.slot` in any analysis of this file: node_beacon.cpp:876/879 label a beacon-DV merge primary/alt regardless of which TABLE was merged, so a same-team beacon's merge into _rt_team reads slot=primary (sim-only telemetry defect, reported not fixed). ASSERT LABELS: 1-4 setup (the homed/off-grid split is REAL, not assumed), 5-9 the T6 origin namespace, 10-19 ★ R3 (the ack returns on the team plane and NO static-plane frame is generated), 21-24 the off-grid control arm. ★★ PROBE MATRIX — MEASURED 2026-07-28 against this exact file, by reverting T6/Part A's stamp_origin team arm to the pre-T6 expression (probe P-T6A): 801 events, **12 of the 24 assertions FAIL** (5,6,7,8,9 origin namespace · 11,12 the ack · 13,14,16 R3 · 19,20 the counts), and every failure carries the literal pre-T6 signature from the §11 measurement: tx_enqueue{origin:101} · r_tx{dst:101,reason:no_route,ttl:1} on TO, 3 of them · ★ rreq_forward{dst:101,origin:220,ttl:15} ON THE STATIC NODE S2, i.e. a TEAM message's ack provoking a STATIC-plane RREQ flood that a static node re-flooded · e2e_ack_tx{dst:101} · send_failed{reason:e2e_ack_timeout} on TH · e2e_ack_rx count 0 where 2 are required. AFTER: 654 events, 0 failures. ★ ALL FOUR control-arm assertions (21-24) HOLD under P-T6A — that is what makes them a control rather than a second copy of the experiment. ⚠ ASSERTS 17 and 18 HOLD UNDER P-T6A TOO and are NOT discriminators — they are standing invariants, recorded honestly: 17 holds because TO's own control-arm DM also RTSes to 210, and 18 because a static route request is a broadcast F, never an RTS. Do not cite either as evidence that T6 works.

commands._c: ★ THE MEASURED CASE: a HOMED member's TEAM-plane -a send. Trailing ' -t' is the only form the parser honours.
CONTROL ARM: the OFF-GRID direction, which already worked pre-T6 and must not regress.
second homed -a, after both directions have converged (the ack path must be repeatable, not first-flight luck)
the route dump asserts 16/17 read (a cmd_reply assertion needs the command to have actually been issued)

expect._c: 1 [setup] TH is genuinely HOMED onto the static host 101 - the precondition for the whole defect
2 [setup] TH's team id is the pinned 210, so every id below is nameable
3 [setup] TO's team id is the pinned 220
4 [setup] ★ TO is genuinely OFF-GRID: it never adopts a home (no link to H1, autoregister off)
5 [T6 origin] ★ THE SLICE: the homed member stamps its TEAM id 210, not its home's STATIC id 101 (pre-T6: origin=101)
6 [T6 origin] ★ and NEVER 101 - one origin namespace per plane, for every -t send in the run
7 [T6 origin] the receiver sees the team id on the wire (inner origin), not the home id
8 [T6 origin] ★ the receiver NEVER sees 101 as a team-DM origin (pre-T6 this was the only value it saw)
9 [T6 origin] delivery carries the team origin all the way to the app push
10 [T6 origin] the SECOND homed -a arrives too (same origin namespace on a repeat send)

11 [R3] ★ the E2E ack RETURNS to the homed sender (pre-T6 it never did in this topology). NB the push kind is `e2e_acked`, not `send_e2e_acked` - the sim renders the firmware's own PushKind table (NodeRuntimeWrapper drainPushes)

12 [R3] ★ and NO ack ever times out on TH (pre-T6: send_failed{e2e_ack_timeout} at +60 s). ⚠ ASSERTED ON THE `send_failed` EMIT, NOT ON THE PUSH, and that is load-bearing: the sim's push emit carries only ctr/dst/kind and DROPS the reason string (slice-gate-method §E, a documented structural blind spot), so a push-keyed form of this assertion would have been unmovable decoration. Measured: keyed on the emit it fails under P-T6A, keyed on the push it does not.

13 [R3] ★★ THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: the acking teammate generates ZERO route requests for the HOME's static id. Pre-T6 this was r_tx{dst:101,reason:no_route} at ttl 1 then ttl 16 x3 - four STATIC-plane RREQ floods produced by a TEAM message's ack, which is the R3 violation ('team-internal routing only, no static infrastructure in the path').
14 [R3] ★ no static-plane RREQ is FORWARDED for the home's id either - the flood is absent, not merely unanswered
15 [R3] the acking teammate does not give up a deferred send (pre-T6: send_deferred_giveup for dst 101)
16 [R3] the ack is emitted as a DM addressed to the sender's TEAM id 210 (e2e_ack_tx carries `dst`, not `to`)

17 [R3] ★ the ack's FIRST HOP is the team id 210 - it left on the team plane, not toward static infrastructure. Deliberately NOT asserted via rt_update.slot: node_beacon.cpp:876/879 mislabel a beacon-DV team merge as slot=primary, so `slot` cannot prove which table a write landed in (BASELINE SCEN finding).
18 [R3] ★ TO never addresses the HOME as a next hop, on any frame in the run - 101 stays invisible to the member (I2)
19 [R3] BOTH homed -a sends are acked (ctr 1 and ctr 3) - the path is stable, not a first-flight coincidence. Counted on e2e_ack_rx because an ack push carries no payload to match on.

20 [R3] ★ zero static route requests of ANY kind on the acking teammate across the whole run: a team-plane message generates no static-plane frame at all, which is the criterion stated more strongly than 'not for dst 101'
21 [control] the off-grid member's own origin is its team id 220 (unchanged by T6 - node_id == team_local_id off-grid)
22 [control] the homed member receives the off-grid teammate's DM
23 [control] ★ the off-grid direction's ack returns too - this arm held BEFORE T6, which is what makes it a control
24 [control] and the homed member's ack for it goes to the off-grid TEAM id 220, never to a static id
